subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Ghostbots and Digital Resurrection
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ghostbots and Digital Resurrection usable.

hook.text: A company offers to create an AI chatbot trained on your dead loved one's texts and voice messages.

buildup.text: AI can now mimic a person's writing style, voice, and conversational patterns using their digital history.

discovery.text: Startups like HereAfter AI and StoryFile let people record interactive messages for their families to use after death.

twist.text: The dead person never consented to being simulated. The ethics of digital resurrection are completely uncharted.

climax.text: AI can recreate how someone talked. It can't recreate who they were. The illusion may do more harm than comfort.

punchline.text: They sound like them. They're not them.

quiz.question: What ethical concern do AI ghostbots raise?
options: The deceased person never consented to being digitally simulated
The technology is too expensive for most families
AI ghostbots are already regulated by law
